hero.tagline: Systems science student and software developer. I build things with .NET, C#, Python, and React — and self-host them.

projects.title: Projects
projects.subtitle: Side projects I've built, shipped, and kept running.

liftlog.title: LiftLog
liftlog.tagline: A workout tracker I built for my own training.
liftlog.description: Plan routines, run sessions with live set tracking, and watch progress charts fill in over time. Installable as a PWA so it works on my phone at the gym.

syncio.title: Syncio
syncio.tagline: Watch videos with friends, in perfect sync.
syncio.description: Create a room, share a 6-character code, and everyone sees the same frame at the same time. Upload your own videos or pull from YouTube and 1000+ other sites. WebSockets keep play, pause, and seek locked across viewers.

foodscraper.title: FoodScraper
foodscraper.tagline: Scrape grocery and recipe data, then visualize it.
foodscraper.description: Pulls prices and nutrition from ICA and recipes from Tasty, stores the results, and runs statistical analysis on top. Charts built with Nivo; scraping built with Selenium and BeautifulSoup.

mognadstrappan.title: mognadstrappan
mognadstrappan.tagline: A maturity-tracking tool built for Trafikverket as a course project.
mognadstrappan.description: Full-stack web app with a React client, a .NET server, a Python microservice, and SQLite. Built on my own time as part of university coursework — not as paid work.

canvas.title: Canvas Assignments (GNOME Extension)
canvas.tagline: Canvas deadlines in my top panel, before I forget them.
canvas.description: A small GNOME Shell extension that shows upcoming assignments and notifies an hour and 30 minutes before each deadline. Because I got tired of missing them.

about.title: About
about.body: I'm a systems science student at Dalarna University, graduating spring 2026. I work part-time as a student employee at Trafikverket (Swedish Transport Administration) and spend my off-hours building and self-hosting side projects. My path into software went through five years as a process operator and internal trainer at Senseair, where I led training in soldering and electronics and built a knowledge-test system from scratch — which is where I learned I liked building things more than assembling them.
